children: The Ministry of Defence has signed an ₹810.79 crore contract with Bharat Dynamics Ltd (BDL) for 160 Satellite Smart Anti-Airfield Weapons (SAT-SAAW) and associated equipment for the Indian Air Force, in another boost to India’s push for indigenous defence manufacturing.
The contract, signed in New Delhi on September 23 in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh, comes under the Buy (Indian-Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured) category.

SAT-SAAW is an air-to-ground precision-guided glide bomb designed to be launched from platforms including the Jaguar, Hawk and Su-30 MKI. The system is capable of engaging enemy airfields from a long stand-off range.

Designed and developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), the weapon will have 60% indigenous content. The programme also involves indigenisation of key sub-systems, including the Initial Measurement Unit, Long Impact Delay Fuse and Twin Store Carrier.

Deliveries are scheduled across 2027-28 and 2028-29. According to the Defence Ministry, the induction of SAT-SAAW will strengthen the operational capabilities of the IAF and bolster the country’s defence preparedness.
The contract adds to BDL’s growing order pipeline at a time when the defence PSU has also reported a sharp improvement in financial performance.
In August, BDL reported more than a six-fold jump in profit to ₹118.8 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, from ₹18.4 crore in the year-ago period.

Revenue from operations more than doubled year-on-year to ₹572.2 crore from ₹247.9 crore, while EBITDA turned positive at ₹83.1 crore, compared with an EBITDA loss of ₹45.4 crore a year earlier. The EBITDA margin stood at 14.5%.

Total income for the quarter was ₹675.7 crore, including ₹103.4 crore of other income, while total expenses stood at ₹510 crore. Profit before tax rose to ₹165.6 crore from ₹23.1 crore in the year-ago period.

BDL has also added to its order book through other defence contracts. In June, the company secured orders worth ₹1,347.71 crore from Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL). These included ₹1,109.37 crore worth of Helina launchers and line-replaceable units, and another ₹238.34 crore for countermeasure dispensing system LRUs. The contracts are to be executed over 24 to 60 months.
BDL, a Ministry of Defence public sector undertaking, manufactures guided missile systems and allied defence equipment for the Indian Armed Forces.
Shares of Bharat Dynamics Ltd closed 0.76% lower at ₹1,162 on the BSE on Wednesday, ahead of the announcement.

title: Bharat Dynamics signs ₹811 crore MoD deal for anti-airfield weapons for IAF
